name: Carson Mansion

dates.altered: The survey: 'There have been minor modifications of the exterior (removal of un- steady exterior chimneys, removal of finials, etc)'; the iron roof cresting on the third floor 'either has been removed or replaced with wood balustrading'. A private club since 1950.
dates.note: Three dates are on the record and none is edited to agree with the others. The node's exemplar and Wikipedia give 1884-1886; the Library's item summary gives '1885- 1886 Initial Construction'; the survey's own historical section says the house was built 'by Newsom Brothers in l885' and 'built for William McKendrie Carson in 1885'.

quotes.page: Cover sheet. Quoted because it is the header that confirms this PDF is HABS No. CA-1911; no page number is printed on it.

quotes.text: Three stories in height, with a lofty off-center tower, the Carson mansion is a flamboyant Stick-Villa with highly personalized orna- mental details. The richly carved interior (especially the stair hall) remains as it was, in large measure.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-1911; no page marker was legible anywhere in the extracted spans of this document.

quotes.text: HISTORICAL INFORMATION Technically, the house under consideration is the "second" Carson House, built for William McKendrie Carson in 1885. The "first" Carson House was a less ambitious residence, across the street from the "second" great mansion.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-1911, Historical Information; no page marker legible.

quotes.text: Solidly built from the ground up, the house has separate foundations for each wall - inside and out. The framing and principal structural and decorative members are entirely of redwood. The principal entrance faces west and the general design of the house is oriented to this view. In type, the Carson House is a Stick-Villa, and reveals the superficial ornamental changes in the Villa of the l880's from such a Villa as the present Governor's Mansion in Sacramento of 1877.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-1911, EXTERIOR; no page marker legible.

quotes.text: There have been minor modifications of the exterior (removal of un- steady exterior chimneys, removal of finials, etc); but the general effect is virtually the same today as it was in the photograph publish- ed in Souvenir of Humboldt County in 1902, when the extremely stark flavor of the first years of the house had been softened by growing plants. The original iron balustrade^ remains on the second floor, encircling the area above the main porch and providing a balcony of great amplitude at this level. The iron cresting on the roofs of the third floor either has been removed or replaced with wood balustrading.
quotes.page: HABS No. CA-1911; no page marker legible.

measurements.name: storey_count
measurements.note: Three storeys plus the tower, which the survey says is 'lofty' and does not dimension.

note: The survey calls this house a 'Stick-Villa' twice and never calls it Queen Anne, which is worth carrying against the node's own exemplar note reading it as 'Queen Anne with Eastlake, Italianate, and Stick elements' -- the 1964 surveyor and the node disagree about the style of the building the node names first, and neither has been edited. Also worth carrying: the survey records that unsteady exterior chimneys were REMOVED, so a chimney count taken off a photograph of this house today is a count of what survived. The 97,000 feet of Primavera wood is a quantity of material rather than a building dimension and is left in the quote rather than parsed into `measurements`. Written 5 Sep 2026 (WP-11.3, Queen Anne and Stick Style cluster).
